# Training report (auto-generated by `ml/train.py`)

> **Read this first.** Crashes and hard negatives are *simulated* (physics model on top of real UCI HAR sensor noise); no public labelled dataset of real phone-sensor crashes exists. Numbers below measure how well the classifier separates scenario families under my modelling assumptions. They are **not** a real-world accuracy claim. Contributed real events (see docs/DATA_FORMAT.md) let the model be retrained on field data.

- Simulated events: 23000 over 23 scenario types (9000 crash / 14000 non-crash); 22224 pass the 3.5 g trigger gate
- **Real data:** 10299 real HAR windows (7.3 h of everyday activity): natural trigger rate 0.000% (0 windows)
- Chosen architecture: MLP (64, 32, 16), L2 alpha=0.01 (best of 4 by scenario-held-out score)
- **Scenario-held-out (6-fold, test scenarios never seen in training):** AUC **0.9934**, crash recall **93.4%**, false-alarm rate **1.00%** at threshold 0.859 (threshold set for <= 1% FPR on those held-out predictions)
- Random split (same scenarios in train and test; optimistic, for comparison only): recall 97.2%, false-alarm 0.12%

For CRASH rows high is good; for no-crash rows low is good. 'passes trigger' below 100% for crashes means the +-8/16 g phone accelerometer never crossed the gate (a real hardware limit).
